inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 20-F: StockBasedComp 188 (core_metrics). Awards are settled with shares bought on-market by the ESOP trusts (5.37m shares FY2026), so there is no separate net-share-settlement tax outflow; EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0 every year.
inputs.fx_note: Model runs in USD (20-F statements, flows, WACC); per-share values converted to AUD at 1/AUDUSD = 1/0.6957 = 1.4374 AUD per USD (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-02T21:30Z). Parity check against the NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 2 ordinary shares): ADR close US$86.07 / 2 = US$43.04 per share vs BHP.AX A$61.21 x 0.6946 (AUDUSD near the ASX close) = US$42.52, a 1.2% gap fully explained by the ADR trading ~14 hours after the ASX close on a +1.7% NYSE day. Direction and quote basis confirmed. refresh_price.py moves the price, not this rate: re-date it when it is refreshed.
inputs.quote_choice: Anchored on the ASX line (BHP.AX, AUD). It is the primary listing, the deepest pool of liquidity and the register most holders own; the NYSE ADR is a 2:1 derivative of it. The unsuffixed intrinsic values are therefore AUD per ordinary share; USD per-share twins are the engine's model-currency values (divide by fx_rate). An ADR holder multiplies the USD per-share value by 2.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T06:18:01Z ASX regular close (Friday session; Saturday valuation date, not an after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 5,081.4m shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (20-F share capital note) plus ~11m dilutive employee awards (diluted WASO 5,089m vs basic 5,078m) = 5,092m. Held FLAT: SBC (0.3% of revenue) is expensed in the flows and awards are satisfied with shares the ESOP trusts buy on market, so the count does not grow. No buyback since the FY2019 off-market tender; the flat count is a modelling convention BHP funds through ESOP purchases, not a repurchase program.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-built, matching the flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 (diversified tier-one miner) -> cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax debt cost ~5.3% (A-rated notes), ~4% after tax, at ~10% of capital -> WACC ~8.5%. No country or commodity premium: cyclicality and China concentration are charged in the scenario flows and the 20% bear weight, once (adaptations 7f). Same WACC in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash payment (principal 978 + interest 194 = 1,172 FY2026; 881 FY2025) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path 1.9%; D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (6,201 - 1,036 = 5,165 FY2026 = 8.8% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT. ALL lease liabilities (3,496, incl. the 735 index-linked freight leases BHP already excludes) are excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI (Escondida 42.5%, Jimblebar 15% and others) folded into the combined cash tax + NCI leakage driver; NO NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibrated to NCI CASH (dividends to NCI 2,355 FY2026 / 1,873 FY2025 / 1,424 FY2024) rather than NCI profit (3,193 / 2,124 / 1,704), because BHP's capex line is 100% consolidated and NCI partners fund their share of Escondida capex out of their profit. FY0 check: model EBIT 26,610 (underlying EBITDA 32,947 + SBC 188 - SBC 188 - leases 1,172 - D&A ex-ROU 5,165); attributable unlevered NOPAT = underlying attributable profit 13,204 + after-tax net finance cost ex-exceptional (855 - 259 = 596) - after-tax lease interest (~136) + NCI profit-vs-dividend gap (~840) = ~14,500 -> leakage 1 - 14,500/26,610 = 45.5%, rounded to 46%. Cash tax alone (income tax + royalty-related tax, ex-exceptional 9,388 on underlying PBT 25,785) runs ~36.4%.
inputs.net_debt_basis: BHP's own FY2026 net debt 8,694 (note 21) less the lease liabilities it contains (3,496 - 735 freight = 2,761) = 5,933 ex-lease net debt. total_debt 24,465 = interest-bearing liabilities ex leases 23,625 + 840 net hedging derivatives BHP counts in net debt; cash 18,532 (cash 7,609 + short-term deposits 10,923). Interest income (604) is NOT stripped from the flows: the company is net DEBT, and the build starts from underlying EBITDA, which excludes finance income anyway.
inputs.notes: MODEL: mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the cyclical/currency/lease/NCI adaptations. BHP is a mature diversified miner (iron ore ~38%, copper ~35-45%, met coal ~15%, potash from mid-CY2027) whose cash flows are a real operating stream, so owner-FCF is the right engine; the cyclicality is handled by building FY2027 off a mid-cycle commodity deck rather than FY2026 actuals. NORMALISATION: (1) Underlying EBITDA (CSV EBITDA column) is the base, so FY2022's US$10.7bn Woodside/petroleum gain, the FY2024 Nickel West and FY2026 US$2.3bn Jansen impairments and all Samarco exceptional charges are outside the flows; (2) FY2026's 56.1% underlying margin is above the FY2017-FY2026 ex-boom (FY21-22) range of 50.7-53.1%, so base runs 52.3-52.8% pre-SBC (~52% post-SBC); (3) FY2027 revenue is set ~6% below FY2026 on the guided 150kt+ copper volume step-down (1,650-1,800kt vs ~2Mt) and price normalisation, landing at ~US$55bn, the FY2023-FY2026 average of US$54.9bn; (4) the Jansen/Escondida capex cycle (~US$11bn/yr guided, ~US$4bn growth) is carried explicitly and tapers to ~12% of revenue (maintenance + growth to support 2% terminal growth) by FY2036, so neither peak capex nor zero growth capex is capitalised. SBC is expensed at 0.32% of revenue; the EBITDA path is grossed up by the same 0.32pp because IFRS underlying EBITDA is already post-SBC (charged once). BRIDGE: ex-lease net debt plus three debt-like claims held outside the flows (equity_bridge): Samarco dam-failure provision, Antamina silver-stream liability, closed-site closure provisions (after tax). Operating-site closure provisions (7,953) are NOT deducted: they fall due at end of mine life and the perpetuity assumes those assets are replaced by reinvestment; that is the one generous judgment in the bridge (~US$1.1/share after tax if deducted).

equity_bridge.item: Samarco dam-failure provision (Brazil Settlement Agreement to 2043 + UK group action)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 20-F provision note (current 1,653 + non-current 3,544). Payments are exceptional items, outside underlying EBITDA, so the stock is deducted once here. Held gross of tax (Brazilian deductibility uncertain). UK stage-2 trial Apr-2027 to Mar-2028 is an unquantified tail either way.

equity_bridge.item: Antamina silver-streaming liability (Wheaton, US$4.3bn upfront Apr-2026)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 20-F note 24, amortised cost. The US$4.3bn cash sits inside the 18,532 cash balance while future silver deliveries (33.75% of Antamina silver, 22.5% after 100Moz, at 20% of spot) are an obligation the historically-calibrated EBITDA path does not charge. Deducted as debt.

equity_bridge.item: Closure and rehabilitation provisions -- closed sites, after tax
equity_bridge.note: Closed-site provision 3,645 (FY2026 20-F note 15) x (1 - 30% Australian tax deduction). Legacy sites produce no revenue but still consume cash (~470/yr total closure spend, outside the EBITDA-built flows).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2023 -> FY2026, a mid-cycle-to-mid-cycle window), cross-checked against guided ~3-4% copper-equivalent volume CAGR to FY2035 plus Jansen potash
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.6% / -0.1%) diverges >30% from EPS CAGR (-8.8% / -2.8%) and from revenue (3.0% / -0.7%). Every 5-year series starts in the FY2021 commodity boom and every EPS series is bent by FY2022's US$10.7bn Woodside gain and the FY2024/FY2026 impairments; equity is held down by a 50-66% payout plus specials. None is a usable growth anchor for a price-taking commodity producer, so the forward path is built from guided volumes and a mid-cycle price deck, not from a CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC; no equity-award taxes, no interest strip because net debt) went 20,453 (FY2021) -> 26,176 (FY2022 peak) -> 11,838 / 11,720 / 9,164 / 11,741 (FY2023-26). The -10.5% 5-yr CAGR is a boom-to-mid-cycle comparison plus the doubling of capex (5.9bn FY2022 -> 9.8bn FY2026 on Jansen), not deterioration of the asset base. The 10-year average owner FCF is ~13.7bn consolidated (~11bn attributable after NCI dividends and leases).

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2027 -6%: guided copper 1,650-1,800kt (vs ~2Mt FY2026) and iron ore 258-269Mt flat, on a mid-cycle deck (iron ore ~US$95/t CFR, copper ~US$9,500/t real) -> ~US$55bn, the FY2023-26 average. FY2028+ ~2% nominal price plus copper-equivalent volume growth: Jansen Stage 1 first potash mid-CY2027 ramping FY2028-30 (4.15Mtpa, ~US$1.4bn revenue at full rate), WAIO >305Mtpa debottleneck from Q4 FY2028, Stage 2 and Escondida New Concentrator (CY2031-32). Copper-eq ~3-4% volume CAGR guidance partly offset by declining Queensland coal; fades to 2.5% by FY2035-36.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin. Underlying (post-SBC) ~52.0% FY2027 rising to ~52.5% as copper and potash grow in the mix -- inside the ex-boom FY2017-FY2026 range (50.7-53.1%), well below FY2026's 56.1% and the FY2021-22 61-62%.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: Purchases of PP&E plus exploration (10,257 FY2026). ~US$10.9bn FY2027-28 per ~US$11bn guidance (Jansen Stage 1 completion + Stage 2, ENC pre-commitment, WAIO), easing as Jansen spend rolls off but held up through FY2031-32 by Escondida New Concentrator (US$5.4-6.3bn 100% basis), then tapering to 12% of revenue (~US$8.6bn by FY2036) vs D&A ex-ROU at 10% -- a 2pp reinvestment gap that funds the 2% terminal growth rather than assuming growth for free.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: Combined leakage on EBIT: ~36.4% income + royalty-related cash tax and the NCI share of cash (~15% of post-tax profit, calibrated to dividends paid to NCI). See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_capture_rationale: Producer: receivables + inventories exceed payables; growth consumes cash and contraction releases it (FY2026 WC outflow 1,657 on a +7.5bn revenue move = ~22%; FY2025 inflow on contraction). -10% of the revenue change is a mid-point that keeps the FY2027 release modest.
base.narrative: Mid-cycle base. Commodity prices revert from FY2026's copper-led high to a mid-cycle deck; the guided FY2027 copper dip is absorbed; Jansen delivers at its revised US$8.4bn Stage 1 cost and ramps over three years; Escondida New Concentrator is sanctioned and built on schedule; China steel holds near 1bn t but does not grow, so iron ore is a flat cash engine while copper and potash supply the growth. Capex stays near US$11bn through the cycle and only normalises in the early 2030s.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 14x terminal owner FCF (~5.2x terminal EBITDA) binds below Gordon (8.5%/2.0% = 15.7x). Low end of the 12-15x cyclical band would double-penalise: the terminal FCF is already a cycle-averaged, mid-cycle figure with growth capex normalised, so the cap only needs to brake Gordon, not price the cycle again. 12x (first draft) implied 4.5x EV/EBITDA, below any through-cycle multiple BHP has traded on. Bull 15x (~5.5x EBITDA), bear 11x (~4.0x).

bull.narrative: Copper supercycle. Electrification, grid build-out and AI/data-centre power demand turn the forecast refined-copper deficit into sustained US$11-12k/t prices; copper (already ~54% of EBITDA) compounds at the guided ~50%-by-mid-2030s volume ambition via Escondida, Spence and Resolution; China steel proves as resilient as FY2026 showed, keeping iron ore near US$100/t; Jansen ramps cleanly into a firm potash market. Revenue holds FY2026's level through the FY2027 copper dip, margins stay at FY2026's ~56%, and the market grants a 13x exit multiple. The leakage rate edges up because more of the profit comes from 57.5%-owned Escondida.

bear.narrative: China plateau turns to decline. Chinese steel output rolls over from ~1bn t as property stays weak, CMRG uses its single-desk buying power to widen discounts on BHP's lower-grade WAIO blends, and Simandou adds seaborne supply, taking iron ore to US$70-80/t; copper eases to ~US$8,500/t as the FY2027 volume dip extends; Jansen overruns again and potash is oversupplied; met coal spreads compress. Revenue falls ~15% to ~US$50bn (FY2025 was 51.3bn), margins settle in the high-40s (still above FY2016's trough thanks to cost-curve position), capex is cut only slowly because Jansen and ENC are committed, and the exit multiple compresses to 10x. Samarco UK stage-2/3 outcomes above the provision would be additional, unmodelled downside.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle: commodity prices revert from FY2026's copper-led high, the guided FY2027 copper dip passes, Jansen ramps at its revised cost, Escondida New Concentrator is built, iron ore is a flat cash engine on a ~1bn t China steel plateau, and the US$11bn capex cycle normalises in the early 2030s.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper supercycle: structural electrification/AI-power demand keeps copper at US$11-12k/t, copper volumes deliver the ~50%-by-mid-2030s ambition, China steel stays resilient, Jansen ramps cleanly, FY2026's ~56% margin holds and the market pays 13x at exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: China rolls over: steel output declines, CMRG squeezes WAIO pricing and Simandou adds supply (iron ore US$70-80/t), copper softens, Jansen overruns into an oversupplied potash market, revenue falls ~15%, margins sit in the high-40s and the exit multiple compresses to 10x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%: commodity mean-reversion is symmetric and China concentration (CMRG dispute) is real, but BHP sits at the bottom of the iron ore and copper cost curves with 13% gearing, so the downside is margin compression, not solvency -- below FMG's 30% because the portfolio is diversified and copper-led. Base 50%: mid-cycle deck with guided volumes. Bull 30%: tilted above the bear because copper is the one commodity in the portfolio with a broadly-held structural deficit thesis and is now the majority of EBITDA, but trimmed from the house 35% because the bull case also needs China steel to hold and Jansen to execute -- several independent things going right.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Read band_position as n/a. SBC is 0.32% of revenue, so house and street differ by under A$1/share and (price - house)/(street - house) evaluates to a degenerate ~2,700% (the build recomputes the field; a null supplied in the Drivers file is overwritten). The price sits far above BOTH bases: the gap is a commodity-deck question, not an SBC-accounting one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value BHP on what its tier-one asset base earns through a commodity cycle, not at the top of one. The base case strips every exceptional item (Woodside gain, Jansen and Nickel West impairments, Samarco charges), builds FY2027 on a mid-cycle price deck with guided volumes, charges the full US$11bn/yr Jansen/Escondida capex cycle explicitly, makes the flows attributable (NCI calibrated to cash paid to Escondida's partners), and deducts the debt-like claims the flows do not carry (Samarco, the Antamina silver stream, closed-site rehabilitation). The gap between that value and the price is the market's commodity-price view; the bull scenario is roughly what the current deck capitalised looks like.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity price deck: a US$10/t move in iron ore or US$1,000/t in copper moves annual EBITDA by roughly US$2.5bn and US$1.5-2bn respectively -- the dominant driver, and the reason a mid-cycle base sits far from a price set off spot.
China / CMRG single-desk buyer leverage over WAIO pricing and the yuan-settlement shift; China takes over half of iron ore shipments.
Jansen potash execution and returns: Stage 1 already US$5.7bn -> ~US$8.4bn with a US$2.3bn impairment; Stage 2 is sanctioned and sits inside the capex path.
Samarco tail: the provision covers the Brazil settlement and a best estimate of the UK group action, but stage-2 (2027-28) and stage-3 outcomes could be materially higher or lower.
Capital allocation: a renewed large acquisition (three Anglo American approaches since 2024) would replace the modelled organic capex path with an acquisition at a control premium.

FX: per-share AUD values move one-for-one with AUD/USD (fx_rate 1.4374); a weaker AUD lifts the AUD value of USD flows and lowers BHP's AUD cost base -- a natural hedge the USD-only model does not capture.
Operating-site closure provisions (7,953 pre-tax) are not deducted; deducting them after tax would lower every scenario by ~US$1.1/share.
